questions: What is the exact definition of a path of length K in this context - does it mean K edges or K vertices?
Can paths share vertices or must all vertices be used exactly once across all paths?
Are the paths required to be simple paths (no repeated vertices) or can they revisit vertices?
What should be the output format if the decomposition is not possible - just "No" or something else?
Is the matrix P required to be filled in row-major order when outputting the solution, or is any valid arrangement acceptable?
Can a path start and end at any vertices, or are there constraints on the endpoints of each path?
What happens if NK is not divisible by K - is this case always impossible or are there exceptions?
Are self-loops or multiple edges between the same pair of vertices allowed in the input tree?

inline_prompts:
You are given a tree with NK vertices. The vertices are numbered 1,2,\dots,NK, and the i-th edge (i=1,2,\dots,NK-1) connects vertices u_i and v_i. Determine whether this tree can be decomposed into N paths, each of length K. More precisely, determine whether there exists an N \times K matrix P satisfying the following:
- P_{1,1}, \dots, P_{1,K}, P_{2,1}, \dots, P_{N,K} is a permutation of 1,2,\dots,NK.
- For each i=1,2,\dots,N and j=1,2,\dots,K-1, there is an edge connecting vertices P_{i,j} and P_{i,j+1}.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N K
u_1 v_1
u_2 v_2
\vdots
u_{NK-1} v_{NK-1}
Output
If it is possible to decompose the tree into N paths each of length K, print Yes.
Constraints
- 1 \leq N
- 1 \leq K
- NK \leq 2 \times 10^5
- 1 \leq u_i < v_i \leq NK
- The given graph is a tree.
- All input values are integers.
